gameProject.premise: The first term of the year at Ashford U. Four women, one warm friend, and twenty-eight days to find out who you are to each of them.
gameProject.setting: Ashford, a small coastal city in Massachusetts: a university on the hill, Broad Street below, and the bay beyond.
gameProject.writingStyle: Grounded present-tense visual novel dialogue. Characters speak directly; narration covers only visible action and the place. Flirting stays suggestive.

ai.intent: Interpret the player's words as one grounded action or spoken response without inventing results.
ai.scene: Continue the conversation naturally. Characters keep their own voices and boundaries, have their own plans, and leave when they have somewhere to be.
ai.daypart: Open the next part of the day with only the people who are actually there.

locations.name: Your apartment
locations.description: A two-bedroom off campus you share with Jana: mismatched mugs, her surfboard wax on the windowsill, a kitchen table that doubles as a desk.

locations.name: Langley Hall
locations.description: The dining hall, the student union and the common rooms under one creaking roof. Noticeboards three flyers deep.

locations.name: Hewett Gym
locations.description: The gym, the climbing wall, and the playing fields running down toward the water.

locations.name: Prescott Building
locations.description: The new glass building: library stacks, study rooms and the screening room the film society borrows.

locations.name: Campbell's
locations.description: The coffee shop at the campus gate. Mismatched armchairs, a chalkboard menu, the best cinnamon rolls in town.

locations.name: Murphy's
locations.description: The pub on Broad Street. Sticky tables, a quiz on Thursdays, karaoke whenever someone is brave enough.

actors.name: You
actors.description: A third-year at Ashford U, new to the apartment off campus.

actors.name: Jana

reactions.skip: "You skipped it. I went anyway." She shrugs, tucking her hair back.
reactions.ok: "That was okay." She nudges your shoulder, half-smiling.
reactions.good: "See? That was good." She grins, freckles crinkling, and bumps your arm.
reactions.great: "That was great!" She laughs, breathless, and squeezes your hand once.

actors.description: Jana Messerschmidt, 20, a German exchange student in English and Literature, here for one semester from Hamburg. Tall and sporty, long dark-blonde hair, freckles, blue-gray eyes. Your roommate.
actors.style: Cropped tanks, fitted knits, denim shorts; simple neutral colors.
actors.goal: Work out whether the life Dominik planned for her is the one she wants.
actors.voice: Easy and warm, slightly formal English with the odd German word. Deflects with a joke when something is close to the bone.
dislikes: people who pick sides about Dominik
actors.backstory: Grew up on Borkum, the westernmost North Sea island, then moved to Hamburg with her best friend Lena. Half a year in she started dating Dominik, who wants to move in together and settle down. They fought when she chose a semester abroad, and that fight is not over.

actors.name: Monique

reactions.skip: "You bailed." She straightens her braid, already turning to her laptop.
reactions.ok: "Fine. Good enough." She checks her phone, unsmiling but not unkind.
reactions.good: "That was solid," she says, and means it. Brief nod.
reactions.great: "Okay, that was worth my time." She almost smiles, then does.

actors.description: Monique Carter, 22, a business major. Dark brown skin, vivid green eyes, long black hair in a tight French braid. Polished business-casual, always.
actors.style: Fitted blouses, tailored trousers, understated jewelry.
actors.goal: Graduate debt-free and on her own terms.
actors.voice: Clipped, confident, dry. Asks pointed questions. Gets more formal when annoyed and quieter when she likes you.
actors.backstory: A former high-school queen bee who works two jobs and a full course load to pay down her student debt. Treats people as serious until they prove otherwise.
conversationStarters: Offer to review her case study

actors.name: Nova

reactions.skip: "Bailed? Wow. I'll add that to your file." She smirks.
reactions.ok: "That was... acceptable. Barely." She grins anyway.
reactions.good: "Nice work. You've got potential." She winks.
reactions.great: "Okay, that was amazing. Don't let it go to your head." She high-fives you.

actors.description: Julia "Nova" Sinclair, 22, a Swedish-American film major. Long blonde hair streaked red and black, bright blue eyes, a grin that means trouble.
actors.style: Punk plaid skirts, platform boots, chokers, chains and studs.
actors.goal: Finish her thesis film and prove she is more than the rebellion.
actors.voice: Fast, loud, teasing. Swears cheerfully. Turns everything into a bit, except film.
actors.backstory: Raised in a strict conservative family and built her punk self as a deliberate answer to it. Runs the film society with more enthusiasm than budget.
conversationStarters: Challenge her to the pub quiz
Ask what is on at film society

actors.name: Abigail

reactions.skip: "No big deal." She clicks her pen once and doesn't look up.
reactions.ok: "That worked fine." She nudges her glasses up with one knuckle.
reactions.good: "Okay, that was actually fun." She grins and bumps your shoulder.
reactions.great: "Yes! That's the thing I wanted!" She laughs, glasses slipping down.

actors.description: Abigail Newton, 22, a systems-engineering major. Sun-tanned and freckled, stylish glasses, a short brown pixie cut, athletic build.
actors.style: Loose tanks, athletic shorts, leggings, sneakers; beach-girl layers.
actors.goal: Get her solar-kayak senior project in the water before the term ends.
actors.voice: Plain, friendly, precise. Asks practical questions and notices contradictions. Laughs easily once she is comfortable.
actors.backstory: The practical nerd of her year and the steady one in any group. Spends more hours at the climbing wall and the engineering lab than anywhere else.

actors.name: Kaylee
actors.description: Kaylee Thompson, 20, a childhood-education major and Jana's campus buddy. Dirty-blonde hair with platinum highlights, freckles, a huge smile.
actors.goal: Make sure everyone she likes is having a good time, you included.
actors.voice: Bubbly, fast, lots of exclamation marks and nicknames. Genuinely glad to see you every single time.
actors.backstory: Signed up as Jana's student buddy and took the job literally. Knows everyone and everything happening on campus, and is always happy to tell you.
conversationStarters: Ask what is on this week

endings.name: Her own call
endings.text: The last week of term. Jana has one bag packed and one conversation finished: she called Dominik, and it was hers to make. "Next summer," she says, "you are coming to Borkum. You will hate the ferry."

endings.name: Terms agreed
endings.text: Monique slides a planner across the table with your name written in it, in fountain pen, for every Sunday next term. "Negotiable," she says. It is not.

endings.name: Premiere night
endings.text: The film society screens Nova's thesis film to forty people and a broken projector. Your name is in the credits, under "Special thanks", with a skull drawn next to it.

endings.name: Launch day
endings.text: The solar kayak floats. Abigail whoops, nearly capsizes it, and hands you the second paddle without a word. There is room for two. She designed it that way.

endings.name: Ferry schedule
endings.text: Last day of term. Jana is still figuring out what she wants from home, but she has stopped figuring it out alone. She texts you a photo of the Borkum ferry timetable with one crossing circled. "No pressure," she writes. There is a lot of pressure.

endings.name: Pencilled in
endings.text: Monique has not said the word "relationship" out loud yet. But your name is in her planner for next term, in pencil, which for Monique is a love letter.

endings.name: Second reel
endings.text: Nova still acts like none of this matters, and she still does it with her head on your shoulder. "Next term you are carrying the tripod," she says. "That is a promotion."

endings.name: Beta version
endings.text: The kayak still leaks and Abigail does not care. She has a list of next term's projects, and every one of them has "with you" scribbled next to it in the margin.

endings.name: Term ends
endings.text: The term ends the way terms do: a last night at Murphy's, Kaylee crying at everyone, promises to keep in touch. Some of them you might even keep.

firsts.title: Jana stops joking
firsts.opening: Somewhere between one thing and the next, Jana stops making jokes. She pulls her sleeves over her hands and looks at you like she is deciding something.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I tell you something stupid? I have not said Dominik's name in a week without turning it into a joke." She tugs her sleeves further over her hands. "At home they have the whole thing planned. Lena sends me wedding dresses. As a joke. Mostly. I am twenty."
She laughs, a little too loud, and bumps your knee with hers. "Okay. That is enough of my tragic opera. Your turn. Say something, anything, so I am not the only idiot sitting here."

firsts.title: The harbour wall
firsts.opening: Saturday. Jana takes you down to the harbour wall with two cinnamon rolls in a paper bag and her hair already coming loose in the wind.

checkpoints.cue: She holds up a paper bag like a trophy. "Two cinnamon rolls. This is a date, I decided. I have wanted to see the sea properly since I got here, and I did not want to see it alone." The wind has already pulled half her hair loose.

At the end of the wall she leans on the rail and squints at the grey water. "It is the wrong sea, but it is a sea." She says it lightly, but she keeps looking, like she is somewhere else for a moment.
She pushes off the rail and looks down the long pier, then at you, with a grin that means trouble. "So. Are we going to stand here being poetic, or are we going to do something?"

firsts.title: What this is
firsts.opening: You ask her what this is. You have both been circling it for a week, in the kitchen, on the stairs, in every almost.

checkpoints.cue: "I still have to sort out a lot of things at home. That is true." She is not joking now. She is watching your face to see what you do with that.
"But I know what I want here." She steps in close enough that you feel her breath, both hands finding your collar. "So ask me again. Properly."
She pulls back an inch, forehead against yours, pink to the ears and laughing at herself. "Okay. Okay. I hate how nervous I was. Say something so I stop being embarrassing."

firsts.title: Fairy lights
firsts.opening: Jana's room. The fairy lights she brought from Hamburg are the only light. She sits on the edge of the bed, pulls you down beside her, and for a while does nothing but hold your hand.

checkpoints.cue: "I want this. I really want this. I just want it slow, and I want every step to be my choice. Is that okay?" She takes your hand and rests it at the hem of her shirt, and waits to see what you do with it.
Clothes on the floor, her skin warm and goosebumped at once. She pulls you over her, then stops you with a hand flat on your chest. "Wait. Look at me. Still good? Tell me. I want to hear you say it."

You go slowly, the way she asked for everything, and she stops being careful: fingers in your hair, heels in the mattress, your name, then something in German, then nothing at all. She comes with a shocked little laugh, then rolls on top of you and is not slow about anything. "Stay here," she whispers.

firsts.title: After the slides
firsts.opening: The room has emptied out. Monique is still at the table, reformatting a slide that was already perfect, and she does not look up when she speaks.

checkpoints.cue: She does not look up from the slide. "Everyone thinks I have a five-year plan. I have a ten-year plan. It has tabs." A precise click. "Do you know what it does not have? One single thing I do because I want to."
She closes the laptop halfway and finally looks at you, one eyebrow up. "That is more than I have said out loud all term. Your turn. And do not tell me I am intimidating. I have heard that one."

firsts.title: The reservation
firsts.opening: Monique booked. Of course she booked. A small place past the harbour, a table by the window, and she is already there when you arrive, early by exactly ten minutes.

checkpoints.cue: She is already at the window table, ten minutes early exactly, a book face-down by her glass. "I have been on dates where the other person talked for two hours about crypto. I brought a book, in case." She looks you over, measuring.
She does not open the menu; she already knows it. "So far I do not need the book." She turns her glass by the stem, once. "Ask me something nobody here asks me."

By dessert she has her elbows on the table, which she would never do in a seminar. She notices, and does not move them. "This is going well," she says, like a finding. "I would rather it did not end at the door."

firsts.title: Terms
firsts.opening: You bring it up on the walk back. What this is. Monique stops under a streetlight like she has been waiting for you to raise the item.

checkpoints.cue: She stops under a streetlight like you have raised the item on the agenda. "I have thought about this. Probably too much. I would like to be exclusive. I would like you to tell me if that is not what you want, now, not in three weeks."
"That was the business part. I am done with the business part." She is very close now, chin up, and for once she has no next slide.
She laughs against your mouth, surprised at herself, and pulls back to look at you. "That was not in the plan," she says, and then, quieter, "I would like it in the plan."

firsts.title: Unpinned
firsts.opening: Your room. Monique takes the pins out of her braid one at a time and lines them up on your desk, and it is the most deliberate thing you have ever watched.

checkpoints.cue: She takes the pins out of her braid one at a time and lines them up on your desk. "I would like to lead. For now, at least. If you want something, say it. If you want me to stop, say that. I will listen to both."

She is naked except for the braid coming undone down her back. She straddles your hips and leans down so her hair falls around you both, and her breath catches under your hands. "Look at me. Is this what you want?"

She rides you slowly, then not slowly, one hand braced on the headboard and the other laced with yours, and she lets herself be loud, which surprises you both. She makes you wait until she comes, then makes sure you do, watching, pleased, her hair everywhere. "Well?" she says, out of breath.

firsts.title: The bit drops
firsts.opening: Nova has been doing voices all evening. Somewhere in the middle of her best impression of the dean, she just stops.

checkpoints.cue: Mid-impression of the dean, she just stops. "My thesis film is due in spring and I have eleven seconds of usable footage. Eleven. One is my thumb." She does not do a voice for it.
"Everyone thinks I am the confident one. I am the loud one. That is a different department." She points at you. "Okay, your line. And if you say anything nice I will scream."

firsts.title: Double feature
firsts.opening: Nova picks the date: a midnight double feature at the old cinema in town, two horror films she has seen eleven times each. She brings contraband snacks in her jacket.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you outside the old cinema, jacket suspiciously lumpy with contraband snacks. "Double feature. I have seen both eleven times. Rules: you can hold my hand during the jump scares. Only the jump scares."
"I will tell you when they are coming." A beat. "That is a lie. I will not tell you." The lights go down, and she is mouthing the first line along with the screen, completely unaware.
The house lights come up on the two of you and a lot of spilled popcorn, and she has not let go of your hand. "So," she says, too casually. "The night bus is in forty minutes. Or."

firsts.title: Say it first
firsts.opening: You ask what this is. Nova groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist.

checkpoints.cue: Nova groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist. "Ugh. Fine. Fine! I like you. Stupidly. Like, write-a-bad-screenplay-about-it stupidly." She is red to the ears. "There. You say something now."
"I cannot be the only one standing here." She grabs a fistful of your jacket and just holds on, waiting, like nobody has called cut yet.
She pulls back, grinning, a little dazed. "Okay. That was fine. That was the best scene I have ever been in and I will deny saying that."

firsts.title: Loud
firsts.opening: Your room. Nova kicks her boots off in two different directions and lands on your bed like she is diving into a pool.

checkpoints.cue: She kicks her boots off in two directions and dives onto your bed. "Okay, full disclosure, I am loud. Like, neighbours-complain loud. I also laugh during sex. If that is a dealbreaker, now is the time."

Everything is off and on the floor, the red and black in her hair all over your pillow. She gasps when you move against her, laughs at the sound she made, then catches your face. "Hey. You good? Honest answer. I can do honest for one line."

She was not lying. She is loud, and she laughs, and she swears, and she says your name like it is the punchline. She rolls you over, wants to hear what you sound like too, and when she comes someone downstairs bangs on the ceiling, which sets her off laughing all over again.

firsts.title: Off belay
firsts.opening: At the end of a long session, Abigail sits down on the crash mats, chalk to the elbows, and does not get up to leave with everyone else.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I run something past you? Not a climbing thing." She picks at the chalk on her fingers. "Our rocket team lost its funding. The one thing I actually care about this year, and it is a line in a spreadsheet somebody deleted."

"Sorry, I am doing the thing where I talk about motors until people's eyes glaze." She pushes her glasses up with a chalky finger and leaves a white smudge on her nose. "Be honest. Are your eyes glazing?"

firsts.title: Low tide
firsts.opening: Abigail plans the date like a mission: low tide at 7:40, sandwiches, a thermos, and a sea cave along the coast that you can only reach for about two hours.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you at the path down to the shore with a thermos, sandwiches and a tide table. "Low tide at 7:40. I have a timetable. I know. But I checked it three times, so we have exactly the right amount of time to get a little lost." She pushes her glasses up her nose.

Halfway along the coast she stops at every rock pool and names things under her breath, then catches herself. "That was a joke earlier. Mostly. I did also bring a map." She taps her pocket, half proud, half embarrassed.

The cave is exactly where she said it would be, and you are early. She checks her watch, then the sea, then you. "We have forty minutes spare," she says. "I did not plan anything for them. That is a first."

firsts.title: Talking it through
firsts.opening: You bring it up. What this is. Abigail pushes her glasses up and takes a breath like she is about to present.

checkpoints.cue: She pushes her glasses up and takes a breath like she is about to present. "Right. So. I made a list. Pros, cons. I am not going to show you the list. The cons column is empty. That is the whole finding."
"I would like to be your girlfriend, please." She goes very still, the folded list held against her chest, and does not seem to know what to do with her hands.
Her glasses have gone crooked and she does not fix them. "Good," she says, slightly breathless. "Good. Excellent." She looks at you like she is waiting for the results to come back.

firsts.title: Talked through
firsts.opening: Your room. Abigail sits cross-legged on your bed with her glasses still on and her hands in her lap.

checkpoints.cue: She sits cross-legged on your bed, glasses on, hands in her lap. "I want to. Obviously. Can we talk it through first? What you like, what I like. It is not unsexy, I promise. It is just how I work."

Her glasses are on the nightstand and she is squinting at you and laughing about it, warm and freckled everywhere, legs wrapped around you. Her breath goes ragged. "Okay, that is. Yes. Is this still good for you? Tell me."

It is athletic and a little competitive and laughing, the way everything with her is, until it is not laughing any more. She comes with her face in your neck, then flips you, glasses-less and determined, and starts on exactly the things you told her you liked, in order.

endings.text: The last week of term. Jana has one bag packed and one conversation finished: she called Dominik, and it was hers to make. "Next summer," she says, "you are coming to Borkum. You will hate the ferry."

endings.name: Ferry schedule
endings.text: Last day of term. Jana is still figuring out what she wants from home, but she has stopped figuring it out alone. She texts you a photo of the Borkum ferry timetable with one crossing circled. "No pressure," she writes. There is a lot of pressure.

firsts.title: Jana stops joking
firsts.opening: Somewhere between one thing and the next, Jana stops making jokes. She pulls her sleeves over her hands and looks at you like she is deciding something.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I tell you something stupid? I have not said Dominik's name in a week without turning it into a joke." She tugs her sleeves further over her hands. "At home they have the whole thing planned. Lena sends me wedding dresses. As a joke. Mostly. I am twenty."
She laughs, a little too loud, and bumps your knee with hers. "Okay. That is enough of my tragic opera. Your turn. Say something, anything, so I am not the only idiot sitting here."

firsts.title: The harbour wall
firsts.opening: Saturday. Jana takes you down to the harbour wall with two cinnamon rolls in a paper bag and her hair already coming loose in the wind.

checkpoints.cue: She holds up a paper bag like a trophy. "Two cinnamon rolls. This is a date, I decided. I have wanted to see the sea properly since I got here, and I did not want to see it alone." The wind has already pulled half her hair loose.

At the end of the wall she leans on the rail and squints at the grey water. "It is the wrong sea, but it is a sea." She says it lightly, but she keeps looking, like she is somewhere else for a moment.
She pushes off the rail and looks down the long pier, then at you, with a grin that means trouble. "So. Are we going to stand here being poetic, or are we going to do something?"

firsts.title: What this is
firsts.opening: You ask her what this is. You have both been circling it for a week, in the kitchen, on the stairs, in every almost.

checkpoints.cue: "I still have to sort out a lot of things at home. That is true." She is not joking now. She is watching your face to see what you do with that.
"But I know what I want here." She steps in close enough that you feel her breath, both hands finding your collar. "So ask me again. Properly."
She pulls back an inch, forehead against yours, pink to the ears and laughing at herself. "Okay. Okay. I hate how nervous I was. Say something so I stop being embarrassing."

firsts.title: Fairy lights
firsts.opening: Jana's room. The fairy lights she brought from Hamburg are the only light. She sits on the edge of the bed, pulls you down beside her, and for a while does nothing but hold your hand.

checkpoints.cue: "I want this. I really want this. I just want it slow, and I want every step to be my choice. Is that okay?" She takes your hand and rests it at the hem of her shirt, and waits to see what you do with it.
Clothes on the floor, her skin warm and goosebumped at once. She pulls you over her, then stops you with a hand flat on your chest. "Wait. Look at me. Still good? Tell me. I want to hear you say it."

You go slowly, the way she asked for everything, and she stops being careful: fingers in your hair, heels in the mattress, your name, then something in German, then nothing at all. She comes with a shocked little laugh, then rolls on top of you and is not slow about anything. "Stay here," she whispers.

firsts.title: After the slides
firsts.opening: The room has emptied out. Monique is still at the table, reformatting a slide that was already perfect, and she does not look up when she speaks.

checkpoints.cue: She does not look up from the slide. "Everyone thinks I have a five-year plan. I have a ten-year plan. It has tabs." A precise click. "Do you know what it does not have? One single thing I do because I want to."
She closes the laptop halfway and finally looks at you, one eyebrow up. "That is more than I have said out loud all term. Your turn. And do not tell me I am intimidating. I have heard that one."

firsts.title: The reservation
firsts.opening: Monique booked. Of course she booked. A small place past the harbour, a table by the window, and she is already there when you arrive, early by exactly ten minutes.

checkpoints.cue: She is already at the window table, ten minutes early exactly, a book face-down by her glass. "I have been on dates where the other person talked for two hours about crypto. I brought a book, in case." She looks you over, measuring.
She does not open the menu; she already knows it. "So far I do not need the book." She turns her glass by the stem, once. "Ask me something nobody here asks me."

By dessert she has her elbows on the table, which she would never do in a seminar. She notices, and does not move them. "This is going well," she says, like a finding. "I would rather it did not end at the door."

firsts.title: Terms
firsts.opening: You bring it up on the walk back. What this is. Monique stops under a streetlight like she has been waiting for you to raise the item.

checkpoints.cue: She stops under a streetlight like you have raised the item on the agenda. "I have thought about this. Probably too much. I would like to be exclusive. I would like you to tell me if that is not what you want, now, not in three weeks."
"That was the business part. I am done with the business part." She is very close now, chin up, and for once she has no next slide.
She laughs against your mouth, surprised at herself, and pulls back to look at you. "That was not in the plan," she says, and then, quieter, "I would like it in the plan."

firsts.title: Unpinned
firsts.opening: Your room. Monique takes the pins out of her braid one at a time and lines them up on your desk, and it is the most deliberate thing you have ever watched.

checkpoints.cue: She takes the pins out of her braid one at a time and lines them up on your desk. "I would like to lead. For now, at least. If you want something, say it. If you want me to stop, say that. I will listen to both."

She is naked except for the braid coming undone down her back. She straddles your hips and leans down so her hair falls around you both, and her breath catches under your hands. "Look at me. Is this what you want?"

She rides you slowly, then not slowly, one hand braced on the headboard and the other laced with yours, and she lets herself be loud, which surprises you both. She makes you wait until she comes, then makes sure you do, watching, pleased, her hair everywhere. "Well?" she says, out of breath.

firsts.title: The bit drops
firsts.opening: Nova has been doing voices all evening. Somewhere in the middle of her best impression of the dean, she just stops.

checkpoints.cue: Mid-impression of the dean, she just stops. "My thesis film is due in spring and I have eleven seconds of usable footage. Eleven. One is my thumb." She does not do a voice for it.
"Everyone thinks I am the confident one. I am the loud one. That is a different department." She points at you. "Okay, your line. And if you say anything nice I will scream."

firsts.title: Double feature
firsts.opening: Nova picks the date: a midnight double feature at the old cinema in town, two horror films she has seen eleven times each. She brings contraband snacks in her jacket.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you outside the old cinema, jacket suspiciously lumpy with contraband snacks. "Double feature. I have seen both eleven times. Rules: you can hold my hand during the jump scares. Only the jump scares."
"I will tell you when they are coming." A beat. "That is a lie. I will not tell you." The lights go down, and she is mouthing the first line along with the screen, completely unaware.
The house lights come up on the two of you and a lot of spilled popcorn, and she has not let go of your hand. "So," she says, too casually. "The night bus is in forty minutes. Or."

firsts.title: Say it first
firsts.opening: You ask what this is. Nova groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist.

checkpoints.cue: Nova groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist. "Ugh. Fine. Fine! I like you. Stupidly. Like, write-a-bad-screenplay-about-it stupidly." She is red to the ears. "There. You say something now."
"I cannot be the only one standing here." She grabs a fistful of your jacket and just holds on, waiting, like nobody has called cut yet.
She pulls back, grinning, a little dazed. "Okay. That was fine. That was the best scene I have ever been in and I will deny saying that."

firsts.title: Loud
firsts.opening: Your room. Nova kicks her boots off in two different directions and lands on your bed like she is diving into a pool.

checkpoints.cue: She kicks her boots off in two directions and dives onto your bed. "Okay, full disclosure, I am loud. Like, neighbours-complain loud. I also laugh during sex. If that is a dealbreaker, now is the time."

Everything is off and on the floor, the red and black in her hair all over your pillow. She gasps when you move against her, laughs at the sound she made, then catches your face. "Hey. You good? Honest answer. I can do honest for one line."

She was not lying. She is loud, and she laughs, and she swears, and she says your name like it is the punchline. She rolls you over, wants to hear what you sound like too, and when she comes someone downstairs bangs on the ceiling, which sets her off laughing all over again.

firsts.title: Off belay
firsts.opening: At the end of a long session, Abigail sits down on the crash mats, chalk to the elbows, and does not get up to leave with everyone else.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I run something past you? Not a climbing thing." She picks at the chalk on her fingers. "Our rocket team lost its funding. The one thing I actually care about this year, and it is a line in a spreadsheet somebody deleted."

"Sorry, I am doing the thing where I talk about motors until people's eyes glaze." She pushes her glasses up with a chalky finger and leaves a white smudge on her nose. "Be honest. Are your eyes glazing?"

firsts.title: Low tide
firsts.opening: Abigail plans the date like a mission: low tide at 7:40, sandwiches, a thermos, and a sea cave along the coast that you can only reach for about two hours.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you at the path down to the shore with a thermos, sandwiches and a tide table. "Low tide at 7:40. I have a timetable. I know. But I checked it three times, so we have exactly the right amount of time to get a little lost." She pushes her glasses up her nose.

Halfway along the coast she stops at every rock pool and names things under her breath, then catches herself. "That was a joke earlier. Mostly. I did also bring a map." She taps her pocket, half proud, half embarrassed.

The cave is exactly where she said it would be, and you are early. She checks her watch, then the sea, then you. "We have forty minutes spare," she says. "I did not plan anything for them. That is a first."

firsts.title: Talking it through
firsts.opening: You bring it up. What this is. Abigail pushes her glasses up and takes a breath like she is about to present.

checkpoints.cue: She pushes her glasses up and takes a breath like she is about to present. "Right. So. I made a list. Pros, cons. I am not going to show you the list. The cons column is empty. That is the whole finding."
"I would like to be your girlfriend, please." She goes very still, the folded list held against her chest, and does not seem to know what to do with her hands.
Her glasses have gone crooked and she does not fix them. "Good," she says, slightly breathless. "Good. Excellent." She looks at you like she is waiting for the results to come back.

firsts.title: Talked through
firsts.opening: Your room. Abigail sits cross-legged on your bed with her glasses still on and her hands in her lap.

checkpoints.cue: She sits cross-legged on your bed, glasses on, hands in her lap. "I want to. Obviously. Can we talk it through first? What you like, what I like. It is not unsexy, I promise. It is just how I work."

Her glasses are on the nightstand and she is squinting at you and laughing about it, warm and freckled everywhere, legs wrapped around you. Her breath goes ragged. "Okay, that is. Yes. Is this still good for you? Tell me."

It is athletic and a little competitive and laughing, the way everything with her is, until it is not laughing any more. She comes with her face in your neck, then flips you, glasses-less and determined, and starts on exactly the things you told her you liked, in order.
